065/**
066 * A numerical axis that uses a logarithmic scale.  The class is an
067 * alternative to the {@link LogarithmicAxis} class.
068 */
069public class LogAxis extends ValueAxis {
070
071    /** The logarithm base. */
072    private double base = 10.0;
073
074    /** The logarithm of the base value - cached for performance. */
075    private double baseLog = Math.log(10.0);
076
077    /** 
078     * The base symbol to display (if {@code null} then the numerical
079     * value of the base is displayed).
080     */
081    private String baseSymbol = null;
082    
083    /** 
084     * The formatter to use for the base value when the base is displayed
085     * as a numerical value.
086     */
087    private Format baseFormatter = new DecimalFormat("0");
088    
089    /**  The smallest value permitted on the axis. */
090    private double smallestValue = 1E-100;
091
092    /** The current tick unit. */
093    private NumberTickUnit tickUnit;
094
095    /** The override number format. */
096    private NumberFormat numberFormatOverride;

111        super(label, new NumberTickUnitSource());

116    /**

128    /**
129     * Sets the base for the logarithm calculation and sends a change event to
130     * all registered listeners.
131     *
132     * @param base  the base value (must be &gt; 1.0).
133     *
134     * @see #getBase()
135     */
136    public void setBase(double base) {
137        if (base <= 1.0) {
138            throw new IllegalArgumentException("Requires 'base' > 1.0.");
139        }
140        this.base = base;
141        this.baseLog = Math.log(base);
142        fireChangeEvent();
143    }

296    /**
297     * Calculates the log of the given value, using the current base.
298     *
299     * @param value  the value.
300     *
301     * @return The log of the given value.
302     *
303     * @see #calculateValue(double)
304     * @see #getBase()
305     */
306    public double calculateLog(double value) {
307        return Math.log(value) / this.baseLog;
308    }
309
310    /**
311     * Calculates the value from a given log.
312     *
313     * @param log  the log value.
314     *
315     * @return The value with the given log.
316     *
317     * @see #calculateLog(double)
318     * @see #getBase()
319     */
320    public double calculateValue(double log) {
321        return Math.pow(this.base, log);
322    }
323    
324    private double calculateValueNoINF(double log) {
325        double result = calculateValue(log);
326        if (Double.isInfinite(result)) {
327            result = Double.MAX_VALUE;
328        }
329        if (result <= 0.0) {
330            result = Double.MIN_VALUE;
331        }
332        return result;
333    }
334
335    /**
336     * Converts a Java2D coordinate to an axis value, assuming that the
337     * axis is aligned to the specified {@code edge} of the {@code area}.
338     *
339     * @param java2DValue  the Java2D coordinate.
340     * @param area  the area for plotting data ({@code null} not 
341     *     permitted).
342     * @param edge  the edge that the axis is aligned to ({@code null} not
343     *     permitted).
344     *
345     * @return A value along the axis scale.
346     */
347    @Override
348    public double java2DToValue(double java2DValue, Rectangle2D area,
349            RectangleEdge edge) {
350
351        Range range = getRange();
352        double axisMin = calculateLog(Math.max(this.smallestValue, 
353                range.getLowerBound()));
354        double axisMax = calculateLog(range.getUpperBound());
355
356        double min = 0.0;
357        double max = 0.0;
358        if (RectangleEdge.isTopOrBottom(edge)) {
359            min = area.getX();
360            max = area.getMaxX();
361        } else if (RectangleEdge.isLeftOrRight(edge)) {
362            min = area.getMaxY();
363            max = area.getY();
364        }
365        double log;
366        if (isInverted()) {
367            log = axisMax - (java2DValue - min) / (max - min)
368                    * (axisMax - axisMin);
369        } else {
370            log = axisMin + (java2DValue - min) / (max - min)
371                    * (axisMax - axisMin);
372        }
373        return calculateValue(log);
374    }
375
376    /**
377     * Converts a value on the axis scale to a Java2D coordinate relative to
378     * the given {@code area}, based on the axis running along the
379     * specified {@code edge}.
380     *
381     * @param value  the data value.
382     * @param area  the area ({@code null} not permitted).
383     * @param edge  the edge ({@code null} not permitted).
384     *
385     * @return The Java2D coordinate corresponding to {@code value}.
386     */
387    @Override
388    public double valueToJava2D(double value, Rectangle2D area,
389            RectangleEdge edge) {
390
391        Range range = getRange();
392        double axisMin = calculateLog(range.getLowerBound());
393        double axisMax = calculateLog(range.getUpperBound());
394        value = calculateLog(value);
395
396        double min = 0.0;
397        double max = 0.0;
398        if (RectangleEdge.isTopOrBottom(edge)) {
399            min = area.getX();
400            max = area.getMaxX();
401        } else if (RectangleEdge.isLeftOrRight(edge)) {
402            max = area.getMinY();
403            min = area.getMaxY();
404        }
405        if (isInverted()) {
406            return max
407                   - ((value - axisMin) / (axisMax - axisMin)) * (max - min);
408        } else {
409            return min
410                   + ((value - axisMin) / (axisMax - axisMin)) * (max - min);
411        }
412    }

425    /**
426     * Adjusts the axis range to match the data range that the axis is
427     * required to display.
428     */
429    @Override
430    public Range calculateAutoRange(boolean adhereToMax) {
431        Plot plot = getPlot();
432        if (plot == null) {
433            return null;  // no plot, no data
434        }
435
436        if (plot instanceof ValueAxisPlot) {
437            ValueAxisPlot vap = (ValueAxisPlot) plot;
438
439            Range r = vap.getDataRange(this);
440            if (r == null) {
441                r = getDefaultAutoRange();
442            }
443
444            double upper = r.getUpperBound();
445            double lower = Math.max(r.getLowerBound(), this.smallestValue);
446            double range = upper - lower;
447
448            // if fixed auto range, then derive lower bound...
449            double fixedAutoRange = getFixedAutoRange();
450            if (adhereToMax && fixedAutoRange > 0.0) {
451                Range aligned = getAutoRangeAlign().align(
452                        new Range(lower, upper), fixedAutoRange);
453                lower = Math.max(aligned.getLowerBound(), this.smallestValue);
454                upper = aligned.getUpperBound();
455            }
456            else {
457                // ensure the autorange is at least <minRange> in size...
458                double minRange = getAutoRangeMinimumSize();
459                if (range < minRange) {
460                    double expand = (minRange - range) / 2;
461                    upper = upper + expand;
462                    lower = lower - expand;
463                }
464
465                // apply the margins - these should apply to the exponent range
466                double logUpper = calculateLog(upper);
467                double logLower = calculateLog(lower);
468                double logRange = logUpper - logLower;
469                logUpper = logUpper + getUpperMargin() * logRange;
470                logLower = logLower - getLowerMargin() * logRange;
471                upper = calculateValueNoINF(logUpper);
472                lower = calculateValueNoINF(logLower);
473            }
474            return new Range(lower, upper);
475        }
476        return null;
477    }

479    /**
480     * Draws the axis on a Java 2D graphics device (such as the screen or a
481     * printer).
482     *
483     * @param g2  the graphics device ({@code null} not permitted).
484     * @param cursor  the cursor location (determines where to draw the axis).
485     * @param plotArea  the area within which the axes and plot should be drawn.
486     * @param dataArea  the area within which the data should be drawn.
487     * @param edge  the axis location ({@code null} not permitted).
488     * @param plotState  collects information about the plot ({@code null} 
489     *         permitted).
490     *
491     * @return The axis state (never {@code null}).
492     */
493    @Override
494    public AxisState draw(Graphics2D g2, double cursor, Rectangle2D plotArea,
495            Rectangle2D dataArea, RectangleEdge edge,
496            PlotRenderingInfo plotState) {
497
498        AxisState state;
499        // if the axis is not visible, don't draw it...
500        if (!isVisible()) {
501            state = new AxisState(cursor);
502            // even though the axis is not visible, we need ticks for the
503            // gridlines...
504            List ticks = refreshTicks(g2, state, dataArea, edge);
505            state.setTicks(ticks);
506            return state;
507        }
508        state = drawTickMarksAndLabels(g2, cursor, plotArea, dataArea, edge);
509        if (getAttributedLabel() != null) {
510            state = drawAttributedLabel(getAttributedLabel(), g2, plotArea, 
511                    dataArea, edge, state);
512            
513        } else {
514            state = drawLabel(getLabel(), g2, plotArea, dataArea, edge, state);
515        }
516        createAndAddEntity(cursor, state, dataArea, edge, plotState);
517        return state;
518    }
519
520    /**
521     * Calculates the positions of the tick labels for the axis, storing the
522     * results in the tick label list (ready for drawing).
523     *
524     * @param g2  the graphics device.
525     * @param state  the axis state.
526     * @param dataArea  the area in which the plot should be drawn.
527     * @param edge  the location of the axis.
528     *
529     * @return A list of ticks.
530     */
531    @Override
532    public List refreshTicks(Graphics2D g2, AxisState state,
533            Rectangle2D dataArea, RectangleEdge edge) {
534        List result = new java.util.ArrayList();
535        if (RectangleEdge.isTopOrBottom(edge)) {
536            result = refreshTicksHorizontal(g2, dataArea, edge);
537        }
538        else if (RectangleEdge.isLeftOrRight(edge)) {
539            result = refreshTicksVertical(g2, dataArea, edge);
540        }
541        return result;
542    }
543    
544    /**
545     * Returns a list of ticks for an axis at the top or bottom of the chart.
546     *
547     * @param g2  the graphics device ({@code null} not permitted).
548     * @param dataArea  the data area ({@code null} not permitted).
549     * @param edge  the edge ({@code null} not permitted).
550     *
551     * @return A list of ticks.
552     */
553    protected List refreshTicksHorizontal(Graphics2D g2, Rectangle2D dataArea,
554            RectangleEdge edge) {
555
556        Range range = getRange();
557        List ticks = new ArrayList();
558        Font tickLabelFont = getTickLabelFont();
559        g2.setFont(tickLabelFont);
560        TextAnchor textAnchor;
561        if (edge == RectangleEdge.TOP) {
562            textAnchor = TextAnchor.BOTTOM_CENTER;
563        }
564        else {
565            textAnchor = TextAnchor.TOP_CENTER;
566        }
567
568        if (isAutoTickUnitSelection()) {
569            selectAutoTickUnit(g2, dataArea, edge);
570        }
571        int minorTickCount = this.tickUnit.getMinorTickCount();
572        double unit = getTickUnit().getSize();
573        double index = Math.ceil(calculateLog(getRange().getLowerBound()) 
574                / unit);
575        double start = index * unit;
576        double end = calculateLog(getUpperBound());
577        double current = start;
578        boolean hasTicks = (this.tickUnit.getSize() > 0.0)
579                           && !Double.isInfinite(start);
580        while (hasTicks && current <= end) {
581            double v = calculateValueNoINF(current);
582            if (range.contains(v)) {
583                ticks.add(new LogTick(TickType.MAJOR, v, createTickLabel(v),
584                        textAnchor));
585            }
586            // add minor ticks (for gridlines)
587            double next = Math.pow(this.base, current
588                    + this.tickUnit.getSize());
589            for (int i = 1; i < minorTickCount; i++) {
590                double minorV = v + i * ((next - v) / minorTickCount);
591                if (range.contains(minorV)) {
592                    ticks.add(new LogTick(TickType.MINOR, minorV, null,
593                            textAnchor));
594                }
595            }
596            current = current + this.tickUnit.getSize();
597        }
598        return ticks;
599    }
600
601    /**
602     * Returns a list of ticks for an axis at the left or right of the chart.
603     *
604     * @param g2  the graphics device ({@code null} not permitted).
605     * @param dataArea  the data area ({@code null} not permitted).
606     * @param edge  the edge that the axis is aligned to ({@code null} 
607     *     not permitted).
608     *
609     * @return A list of ticks.
610     */
611    protected List refreshTicksVertical(Graphics2D g2, Rectangle2D dataArea,
612            RectangleEdge edge) {
613
614        Range range = getRange();
615        List ticks = new ArrayList();
616        Font tickLabelFont = getTickLabelFont();
617        g2.setFont(tickLabelFont);
618        TextAnchor textAnchor;
619        if (edge == RectangleEdge.RIGHT) {
620            textAnchor = TextAnchor.CENTER_LEFT;
621        }
622        else {
623            textAnchor = TextAnchor.CENTER_RIGHT;
624        }
625
626        if (isAutoTickUnitSelection()) {
627            selectAutoTickUnit(g2, dataArea, edge);
628        }
629        int minorTickCount = this.tickUnit.getMinorTickCount();
630        double unit = getTickUnit().getSize();
631        double index = Math.ceil(calculateLog(getRange().getLowerBound()) 
632                / unit);
633        double start = index * unit;
634        double end = calculateLog(getUpperBound());
635        double current = start;
636        boolean hasTicks = (this.tickUnit.getSize() > 0.0)
637                           && !Double.isInfinite(start);
638        while (hasTicks && current <= end) {
639            double v = calculateValueNoINF(current);
640            if (range.contains(v)) {
641                ticks.add(new LogTick(TickType.MAJOR, v, createTickLabel(v),
642                        textAnchor));
643            }
644            // add minor ticks (for gridlines)
645            double next = Math.pow(this.base, current
646                    + this.tickUnit.getSize());
647            for (int i = 1; i < minorTickCount; i++) {
648                double minorV = v + i * ((next - v) / minorTickCount);
649                if (range.contains(minorV)) {
650                    ticks.add(new LogTick(TickType.MINOR, minorV, null,
651                            textAnchor));
652                }
653            }
654            current = current + this.tickUnit.getSize();
655        }
656        return ticks;
657    }

659    /**
660     * Selects an appropriate tick value for the axis.  The strategy is to
661     * display as many ticks as possible (selected from an array of 'standard'
662     * tick units) without the labels overlapping.
663     *
664     * @param g2  the graphics device ({@code null} not permitted).
665     * @param dataArea  the area defined by the axes ({@code null} not 
666     *     permitted).
667     * @param edge  the axis location ({@code null} not permitted).
668     */
669    protected void selectAutoTickUnit(Graphics2D g2, Rectangle2D dataArea,
670            RectangleEdge edge) {
671        if (RectangleEdge.isTopOrBottom(edge)) {
672            selectHorizontalAutoTickUnit(g2, dataArea, edge);
673        }
674        else if (RectangleEdge.isLeftOrRight(edge)) {
675            selectVerticalAutoTickUnit(g2, dataArea, edge);
676        }
677    }
678
679    /**
680     * Selects an appropriate tick value for the axis.  The strategy is to
681     * display as many ticks as possible (selected from an array of 'standard'
682     * tick units) without the labels overlapping.
683     *
684     * @param g2  the graphics device.
685     * @param dataArea  the area defined by the axes.
686     * @param edge  the axis location.
687     */
688    protected void selectHorizontalAutoTickUnit(Graphics2D g2,
689            Rectangle2D dataArea, RectangleEdge edge) {
690
691        // select a tick unit that is the next one bigger than the current
692        // (log) range divided by 50
693        Range range = getRange();
694        double logAxisMin = calculateLog(Math.max(this.smallestValue, 
695                range.getLowerBound()));
696        double logAxisMax = calculateLog(range.getUpperBound());
697        double size = (logAxisMax - logAxisMin) / 50;
698        TickUnitSource tickUnits = getStandardTickUnits();
699        TickUnit candidate = tickUnits.getCeilingTickUnit(size);
700        TickUnit prevCandidate = candidate;
701        boolean found = false;
702        while (!found) {
703        // while the tick labels overlap and there are more tick sizes available,
704            // choose the next bigger label
705            this.tickUnit = (NumberTickUnit) candidate;
706            double tickLabelWidth = estimateMaximumTickLabelWidth(g2, 
707                    candidate);
708            // what is the available space for one unit?
709            double candidateWidth = exponentLengthToJava2D(candidate.getSize(), 
710                    dataArea, edge);
711            if (tickLabelWidth < candidateWidth) {
712                found = true;
713            } else if (Double.isNaN(candidateWidth)) {
714                candidate = prevCandidate;
715                found = true;
716            } else {
717                prevCandidate = candidate;
718                candidate = tickUnits.getLargerTickUnit(prevCandidate);
719                if (candidate.equals(prevCandidate)) {
720                    found = true;  // there are no more candidates
721                }
722            }
723        } 
724        setTickUnit((NumberTickUnit) candidate, false, false);
725    }
726
727    /**
728     * Converts a length in data coordinates into the corresponding length in
729     * Java2D coordinates.
730     *
731     * @param length  the length.
732     * @param area  the plot area.
733     * @param edge  the edge along which the axis lies.
734     *
735     * @return The length in Java2D coordinates.
736     */
737    public double exponentLengthToJava2D(double length, Rectangle2D area,
738                                RectangleEdge edge) {
739        double one = valueToJava2D(calculateValueNoINF(1.0), area, edge);
740        double l = valueToJava2D(calculateValueNoINF(length + 1.0), area, edge);
741        return Math.abs(l - one);
742    }
743
744    /**
745     * Selects an appropriate tick value for the axis.  The strategy is to
746     * display as many ticks as possible (selected from an array of 'standard'
747     * tick units) without the labels overlapping.
748     *
749     * @param g2  the graphics device.
750     * @param dataArea  the area in which the plot should be drawn.
751     * @param edge  the axis location.
752     */
753    protected void selectVerticalAutoTickUnit(Graphics2D g2, 
754            Rectangle2D dataArea, RectangleEdge edge) {
755        // select a tick unit that is the next one bigger than the current
756        // (log) range divided by 50
757        Range range = getRange();
758        double logAxisMin = calculateLog(Math.max(this.smallestValue, 
759                range.getLowerBound()));
760        double logAxisMax = calculateLog(range.getUpperBound());
761        double size = (logAxisMax - logAxisMin) / 50;
762        TickUnitSource tickUnits = getStandardTickUnits();
763        TickUnit candidate = tickUnits.getCeilingTickUnit(size);
764        TickUnit prevCandidate = candidate;
765        boolean found = false;
766        while (!found) {
767        // while the tick labels overlap and there are more tick sizes available,
768            // choose the next bigger label
769            this.tickUnit = (NumberTickUnit) candidate;
770            double tickLabelHeight = estimateMaximumTickLabelHeight(g2);
771            // what is the available space for one unit?
772            double candidateHeight = exponentLengthToJava2D(candidate.getSize(), 
773                    dataArea, edge);
774            if (tickLabelHeight < candidateHeight) {
775                found = true;
776            } else if (Double.isNaN(candidateHeight)) {
777                candidate = prevCandidate;
778                found = true;
779            } else {
780                prevCandidate = candidate;
781                candidate = tickUnits.getLargerTickUnit(prevCandidate);
782                if (candidate.equals(prevCandidate)) {
783                    found = true;  // there are no more candidates
784                }
785            }
786        } 
787        setTickUnit((NumberTickUnit) candidate, false, false);
788    }
789
790    /**
791     * Creates a tick label for the specified value based on the current
792     * tick unit (used for formatting the exponent).
793     *
794     * @param value  the value.
795     *
796     * @return The label.
797     */
798    protected AttributedString createTickLabel(double value) {
799        if (this.numberFormatOverride != null) {
800            String text = this.numberFormatOverride.format(value);
801            AttributedString as = new AttributedString(text);
802            as.addAttribute(TextAttribute.FONT, getTickLabelFont());
803            return as;
804        } else {
805            String baseStr = this.baseSymbol;
806            if (baseStr == null) {
807                baseStr = this.baseFormatter.format(this.base);
808            }
809            double logy = calculateLog(value);
810            String exponentStr = getTickUnit().valueToString(logy);
811            AttributedString as = new AttributedString(baseStr + exponentStr);
812            as.addAttributes(getTickLabelFont().getAttributes(), 0, (baseStr 
813                    + exponentStr).length());
814            as.addAttribute(TextAttribute.SUPERSCRIPT, 
815                    TextAttribute.SUPERSCRIPT_SUPER, baseStr.length(), 
816                    baseStr.length() + exponentStr.length());
817            return as;
818        }
819    }
820
821    /**
822     * Estimates the maximum tick label height.
823     *
824     * @param g2  the graphics device.
825     *
826     * @return The maximum height.
827     */
828    protected double estimateMaximumTickLabelHeight(Graphics2D g2) {
829        RectangleInsets tickLabelInsets = getTickLabelInsets();
830        double result = tickLabelInsets.getTop() + tickLabelInsets.getBottom();
831
832        Font tickLabelFont = getTickLabelFont();
833        FontRenderContext frc = g2.getFontRenderContext();
834        result += tickLabelFont.getLineMetrics("123", frc).getHeight();
835        return result;
836    }
837
838    /**
839     * Estimates the maximum width of the tick labels, assuming the specified
840     * tick unit is used.
841     * <P>
842     * Rather than computing the string bounds of every tick on the axis, we
843     * just look at two values: the lower bound and the upper bound for the
844     * axis.  These two values will usually be representative.
845     *
846     * @param g2  the graphics device.
847     * @param unit  the tick unit to use for calculation.
848     *
849     * @return The estimated maximum width of the tick labels.
850     */
851    protected double estimateMaximumTickLabelWidth(Graphics2D g2, 
852            TickUnit unit) {
853
854        RectangleInsets tickLabelInsets = getTickLabelInsets();
855        double result = tickLabelInsets.getLeft() + tickLabelInsets.getRight();
856
857        if (isVerticalTickLabels()) {
858            // all tick labels have the same width (equal to the height of the
859            // font)...
860            FontRenderContext frc = g2.getFontRenderContext();
861            LineMetrics lm = getTickLabelFont().getLineMetrics("0", frc);
862            result += lm.getHeight();
863        }
864        else {
865            // look at lower and upper bounds...
866            Range range = getRange();
867            double lower = range.getLowerBound();
868            double upper = range.getUpperBound();
869            AttributedString lowerStr = createTickLabel(lower);
870            AttributedString upperStr = createTickLabel(upper);
871            double w1 = AttrStringUtils.getTextBounds(lowerStr, g2).getWidth();
872            double w2 = AttrStringUtils.getTextBounds(upperStr, g2).getWidth();
873            result += Math.max(w1, w2);
874        }
875        return result;
876    }
877
878    /**
879     * Zooms in on the current range.
880     *
881     * @param lowerPercent  the new lower bound.
882     * @param upperPercent  the new upper bound.
883     */
884    @Override
885    public void zoomRange(double lowerPercent, double upperPercent) {
886        Range range = getRange();
887        double start = range.getLowerBound();
888        double end = range.getUpperBound();
889        double log1 = calculateLog(start);
890        double log2 = calculateLog(end);
891        double length = log2 - log1;
892        Range adjusted;
893        if (isInverted()) {
894            double logA = log1 + length * (1 - upperPercent);
895            double logB = log1 + length * (1 - lowerPercent);
896            adjusted = new Range(calculateValueNoINF(logA), 
897                    calculateValueNoINF(logB));
898        }
899        else {
900            double logA = log1 + length * lowerPercent;
901            double logB = log1 + length * upperPercent;
902            adjusted = new Range(calculateValueNoINF(logA), 
903                    calculateValueNoINF(logB));
904        }
905        setRange(adjusted);
906    }
907
908    /**
909     * Slides the axis range by the specified percentage.
910     *
911     * @param percent  the percentage.
912     */
913    @Override
914    public void pan(double percent) {
915        Range range = getRange();
916        double lower = range.getLowerBound();
917        double upper = range.getUpperBound();
918        double log1 = calculateLog(lower);
919        double log2 = calculateLog(upper);
920        double length = log2 - log1;
921        double adj = length * percent;
922        log1 = log1 + adj;
923        log2 = log2 + adj;
924        setRange(calculateValueNoINF(log1), calculateValueNoINF(log2));
925    }
926    
927    /**
928     * Increases or decreases the axis range by the specified percentage about
929     * the central value and sends an {@link AxisChangeEvent} to all registered
930     * listeners.
931     * <P>
932     * To double the length of the axis range, use 200% (2.0).
933     * To halve the length of the axis range, use 50% (0.5).
934     *
935     * @param percent  the resize factor.
936     *
937     * @see #resizeRange(double, double)
938     */
939    @Override
940    public void resizeRange(double percent) {
941        Range range = getRange();
942        double logMin = calculateLog(range.getLowerBound());
943        double logMax = calculateLog(range.getUpperBound());
944        double centralValue = calculateValueNoINF((logMin + logMax) / 2.0);
945        resizeRange(percent, centralValue);
946    }
947
948    @Override
949    public void resizeRange(double percent, double anchorValue) {
950        resizeRange2(percent, anchorValue);
951    }
952
953    /**
954     * Resizes the axis length to the specified percentage of the current
955     * range and sends a change event to all registered listeners.  If 
956     * {@code percent} is greater than 1.0 (100 percent) then the axis
957     * range is increased (which has the effect of zooming out), while if the
958     * {@code percent} is less than 1.0 the axis range is decreased 
959     * (which has the effect of zooming in).  The resize occurs around an 
960     * anchor value (which may not be in the center of the axis).  This is used
961     * to support mouse wheel zooming around an arbitrary point on the plot.
962     * <br><br>
963     * This method is overridden to perform the percentage calculations on the
964     * log values (which are linear for this axis).
965     * 
966     * @param percent  the percentage (must be greater than zero).
967     * @param anchorValue  the anchor value.
968     */
969    @Override
970    public void resizeRange2(double percent, double anchorValue) {
971        if (percent > 0.0) {
972            double logAnchorValue = calculateLog(anchorValue);
973            Range range = getRange();
974            double logAxisMin = calculateLog(range.getLowerBound());
975            double logAxisMax = calculateLog(range.getUpperBound());
976
977            double left = percent * (logAnchorValue - logAxisMin);
978            double right = percent * (logAxisMax - logAnchorValue);
979            
980            double upperBound = calculateValueNoINF(logAnchorValue + right);
981            Range adjusted = new Range(calculateValueNoINF(
982                    logAnchorValue - left), upperBound);
983            setRange(adjusted);
984        }
985        else {
986            setAutoRange(true);
987        }
988    }

990    /**
991     * Tests this axis for equality with an arbitrary object.
992     *
993     * @param obj  the object ({@code null} permitted).
994     *
995     * @return A boolean.
996     */
997    @Override
998    public boolean equals(Object obj) {
999        if (obj == this) {
1000            return true;
1001        }
1002        if (!(obj instanceof LogAxis)) {
1003            return false;
1004        }
1005        LogAxis that = (LogAxis) obj;
1006        if (this.base != that.base) {
1007            return false;
1008        }
1009        if (!Objects.equals(this.baseSymbol, that.baseSymbol)) {
1010            return false;
1011        }
1012        if (!this.baseFormatter.equals(that.baseFormatter)) {
1013            return false;
1014        }
1015        if (this.smallestValue != that.smallestValue) {
1016            return false;
1017        }
1018        if (!Objects.equals(this.numberFormatOverride, 
1019                that.numberFormatOverride)) {
1020            return false;
1021        }
1022        return super.equals(obj);
1023    }

1025    /**
1026     * Returns a hash code for this instance.
1027     *
1028     * @return A hash code.
1029     */
1030    @Override
1031    public int hashCode() {
1032        int result = 193;
1033        long temp = Double.doubleToLongBits(this.base);
1034        result = 37 * result + (int) (temp ^ (temp >>> 32));
1035        temp = Double.doubleToLongBits(this.smallestValue);
1036        result = 37 * result + (int) (temp ^ (temp >>> 32));
1037        if (this.numberFormatOverride != null) {
1038            result = 37 * result + this.numberFormatOverride.hashCode();
1039        }
1040        result = 37 * result + this.tickUnit.hashCode();
1041        return result;
1042    }
